Subject: Post-call recap & next steps (model fit / evals)

Hi Anita — great to meet today. Thanks for walking us through FinAnalytics' use case (real-time client summarization + sentiment flags for multi-tenant dashboards). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

TL;DR: We think Redwood can meet your latency and quality targets with a medium-sized tuned model + prefix KV caching. We attached the sample prompt set you mentioned and a short mapping of prompts -> evaluation slices.

Call notes / asks:
- Target QPS: 150 peak (bursts to 300), target p99 latency <= 450ms for 512-token responses
- Data constraints: PII redaction before sending; cannot persist raw transcripts longer than 48h
- Priority: precision on entity extraction and sentiment for compliance flags; acceptable small hit on generative fluency

Recommended next steps (suggested owners):
1) We’ll run a focused model-fit benchmark against your prompt set (Marissa) — deliverable: per-model TPS, latency percentiles, and QA samples (3 business days)
2) Share Redwood-verified performance profiles + tuning knobs for the recommended model variants (Alex)
3) Legal/procurement intro to align on data handling and contract timing (Dylan / Carlos)

Attachments:
- finanalytics-map-v1-prompt-set.zip (sample prompts + expected labels)
- redwood-benchmark-2026-q1.pdf (Redwood-verified model perf snapshot — excerpt)

Notes about fit: based on your prompts, our initial hypothesis is to try: neo-7b-int8 (cost-friendly), neo-13b-q4 (if you need higher entity precision). We'll include both in the benchmark and call out quality regressions vs your golden set.

Next meeting: suggest Tue 2026-03-31 10:00am PT for a 30-min checkpoint after we run the first pass. Please confirm.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Redwood benchmark draft + verified profiles (neo-7b / neo-13b)

Hi Anita — thanks for the prompt set; we started the benchmark run this morning against your sample prompts. Sharing the initial artifacts and a short interpretation below: 

Artifacts (shared):
- Redwood-verified performance snapshot (attached: redwood-benchmark-2026-q1.pdf)
- Full run & examples: https://drive.redwood-inference.com/shared/finanalytics/benchmarks/2026-q1
- Model variants tested: neo-7b-int8, neo-13b-q4f16 (quantized), neo-70b-cpu-sim (control)

Quick highlights:
- neo-7b-int8: median latency (512 toks): 220ms; p95: 380ms; p99: 510ms; sustained TPS (concurrent workers): ~180
- neo-13b-q4f16: median latency (512 toks): 420ms; p95: 670ms; p99: 920ms; sustained TPS: ~90
- Our autoscaling profiler suggests prefix KV caching will improve p95/p99 by ~15-30% on repeat prompts (relevant for dashboard refreshes)

Quality notes:
- On your entity extraction slices, neo-13b shows a ~6-8% higher F1 vs neo-7b (particularly on company names and fine-grained sentiment), but neo-7b with targeted prompt engineering reduces the gap for many examples
- Flagged a potential quality regression on longer multi-paragraph client notes for neo-7b (examples in Drive under /regressions). We recommend validating on your full golden set; if regressions matter, we can try nucleus-sampling tweaks and a light fine-tune on labeled examples.

Next steps we propose:
1) We’ll run the golden-set regression comparison you’ll send (Marissa) — ETA 48 hours after receipt
2) If you want to prioritize latency & cost, neo-7b-int8 + caching + prompt optimizations is the default recommendation
3) If entity precision is must-have, we’ll prioritize neo-13b-q4f16 and run a short fine-tune experiment (scope: 1k labeled examples) and share cost/quality delta

Links for your teams: 
- Benchmark run results: https://drive.redwood-inference.com/shared/finanalytics/benchmarks/2026-q1/results.csv
- Verified performance profile page: https://app.redwood-inference.com/models/verified#model-neo-7b (see TPS and latency percentiles in the telemetry tab)

I attached the PDF snapshot for quick review. Let me know if you'd like a short walkthrough of the Drive artifacts during Tue's call — happy to share screen and walk through the regressions and tuned prompt examples.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
